rejection_findings.finding: The block misreads the Greek cook as a butcher and misdescribes the action as butchering.

revisions.title: When the cook becomes the object of his craft
revisions.body: Dionysodorus slides from a cook’s activity to the cook as its object. Socrates agrees that the μάγειρος performs the relevant work: slaughtering, skinning, cutting up, boiling, and roasting. Dionysodorus then treats that agreement as permission to apply the same sequence to the cook himself. The trap changes the relation between craft and patient while leaving the craft’s description in place.
